You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the eighth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
[Image: An isosceles triangle. The left angle is labeled "A", the top angle is labeled "C", and the right angle is labeled "B". AC and CB are equal in length. AB is the base. A line is drawn from "C" to a point "X" on the base of the triangle. The line forms a right angle with the base.]

In this triangle:

AC = BC

AB is twice as long as CX.

What is the size of angle B?

Answer: ____ °

Figure, described in words:
An isosceles triangle ABC with horizontal base AB and apex vertex C above it. Side AC and side BC appear equal in length. A vertical line segment CX is drawn from vertex C perpendicular to the base AB at point X, indicated by a square right-angle mark on the right side of segment CX at point X.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Since AB is twice CX, and CX is the altitude from C to base AB, let the length of CX be h and AB = 2h. Since triangle ABC is isosceles with AC = BC and CX perpendicular to AB, X is the midpoint of AB, so AX = XB = h. Then in right triangle AXC, tan(angle A) = CX/AX = h/h = 1, so angle A = 45°. Because AC = BC, angle B = angle A = 45°. Check: angles sum 45 + 45 + 90 = 180, consistent. Answer: 45°
